tagline: City of three mists at the end of the winding road
introHtml:
Mae Hong Son sits on the far western edge of Thailand against the Myanmar border, and getting there means driving through hundreds of curves. Once you arrive, you find a small town in a valley where mist lingers almost year-round, Shan temples with tiered roofs, and a mix of Shan, Karen, and several hill-tribe communities living side by side.

Most people stop in Pai first, then carry on to Pang Ung, the Mexican sunflower fields, or into Mae Hong Son town itself. This is a place for people who like to drive slowly, take their time, and don't mind the cold.
bestTime: November–February, cold and misty. The Mexican sunflower fields bloom in November (avoid March–April, when there's haze and smoke)

highlights.name: Pai
highlights.blurb: A small town in a valley with a walking street, riverside cafes, and mountain-view stays. It's the first stop for most people heading up to Mae Hong Son

highlights.name: Pang Ung
highlights.blurb: A reservoir set in a pine forest with mist drifting over the water in the morning. People call it the Switzerland of Thailand

highlights.name: Mae Hong Son town
highlights.blurb: A small town around Nong Jong Kham lake, with Wat Jong Kham and Wat Jong Klang reflected in the water and a Shan-style morning market

highlights.name: Doi Mae U Kho sunflower fields
highlights.blurb: A hillside where yellow Mexican sunflowers cover the slopes in November, in Khun Yuam district

highlights.name: Tham Lod and Ban Jabo
highlights.blurb: A large cave in Pang Mapha district where you ride a bamboo raft through, plus a noodle shop on the cliff edge at Ban Jabo

highlights.name: Ban Rak Thai
highlights.blurb: A Yunnanese Chinese village along the border, with tea plantations, earthen houses, and Yunnan food to eat

foodScene.name: Khao soi and nam ngiao
foodScene.note: Basic northern dishes you can find all over town. The khao soi here has a deep, Shan-style curry paste flavor

foodScene.name: Shan food
foodScene.note: Fermented soybean, Shan nam phrik ong, Shan-style hung lay curry, and nam ngiao rice noodles — all reflecting the town's Shan roots

foodScene.name: Khanom jeen nam ngiao and rice noodles
foodScene.note: A popular market breakfast, topped with nam ngiao broth and eaten with fresh vegetables and pork crackling

foodScene.name: Yunnan food at Ban Rak Thai
foodScene.note: Aged pork, pork knuckle with mantou buns, and chicken stewed with Chinese herbs, eaten with tea grown in the village

foodScene.name: Noodles at Ban Jabo
foodScene.note: Hot noodles eaten with a cliff view in Pang Mapha — the kind of meal drivers passing through have to stop for

foodScene.name: Cafes and coffee in Pai
foodScene.note: Pai has plenty of riverside and garden coffee shops using beans from the surrounding hills, great for an early morning while the mist hasn't lifted

foodScene.name: Fermented soybean and local dried goods
foodScene.note: Grilled fermented soybean sheets to snack on, plus dried goods from the morning market — classic Mae Hong Son souvenirs

foodScene.name: Sai Yut morning market
foodScene.note: A morning market in town with rice noodles, local sweets, and ready-made Shan dishes

attractions.name: Wat Jong Kham – Wat Jong Klang
attractions.blurb: A pair of Shan temples beside Nong Jong Kham lake in the town center, with tiered roofs that reflect beautifully in the water in the evening and at night

attractions.name: Pang Ung
attractions.blurb: A reservoir in a pine forest in Muang district, with mist and a lake that mirrors the pines in the early morning

attractions.name: Doi Mae U Kho sunflower fields
attractions.blurb: Fields of yellow Mexican sunflowers on a hillside in Khun Yuam district, blooming in November

attractions.name: Tham Lod
attractions.blurb: A large cave with a stream running through it in Pang Mapha district. Ride a bamboo raft to see the stalactites, stalagmites, and ancient wooden coffins

attractions.name: Pai
attractions.blurb: A small town with a walking street, cafes, and a historic bridge — a rest stop for people touring the north

attractions.name: Ban Rak Thai
attractions.blurb: A Yunnanese Chinese village along the border, with tea plantations, earthen houses, and Yunnan food to try

attractions.name: Phra That Doi Kong Mu
attractions.blurb: A pagoda on a hill above town, with a high view over the whole valley of Mae Hong Son

attractions.name: Ban Jabo
attractions.blurb: A Karen village on a ridge in Pang Mapha, with a noodle shop overlooking the cliff and a sea of mist
